clue.text: Gas, then talk back, as one full of hot air

parts.note: gas in the sense of wind, as in flatulence or bluster

indicators.note: back tells us the word for talk is read in the other direction

parts.note: to gab is to talk idly

explanation.surface: Someone gasses on and answers back, the very picture of a bore full of hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word for talk around; 'Gas' looks like a verb but is a noun meaning wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who talks endlessly and emptily is a windbag, a synonym for a bore full of hot air.

clue.text: Artist's break from action?

parts.note: a break from war is a holiday, a hol, so the pop artist splits as war plus hol

explanation.surface: An artist taking a rest from the action.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Warhol was the American pop artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol, the pop artist, whose name splits as war (action) and hol (break).

clue.text: Recess that is a lot of fun

parts.note: a nook is a small recess or corner
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: An alcove that turns out to be great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: IE is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nookie is slang for sex, humorously described as a lot of fun.

clue.text: As Spooner might say, perhaps folder required for parents' assistant

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don, swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: maybe means perhaps
a binder is a folder for papers

explanation.surface: Spooner tells parents that a folder might be just what they need.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of MAYBE BINDER gives BABY MINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby-minder looks after a baby for working parents, helping them out.

clue.text: Device requiring doctrine to cut energy

indicators.note: to cut means the doctrine slices into the word for energy

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
an ism is a doctrine or ideology

explanation.surface: A gadget needs some ideology to cut its power usage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' places the doctrine inside the energy word; 'Device' is the definition, not a contrivance in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo is an informal word for a gadget or contraption.

clue.text: Great success? No sir

definitions.meaning: a ... is a fine victory, a great success
Fred ..., former RBS banker, was stripped of his knighthood in 2012, so is no longer Sir

explanation.surface: A clipped exchange: someone asks if it was a triumph and is told no, sir.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Goodwin led the Royal Bank of Scotland before its 2008 collapse and had his knighthood annulled, hence 'No sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase splits as good plus win, a victory that is great, while the banker lost his title of Sir.

clue.text: Fix up starter of pilau with reduced packaging. Spices strong with it?

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for fix is read upward, so backwards

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly

indicators.note: packaging means the reduced word wraps around the other letter

parts.note: lower means reduced

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cook rigs a pilau with less packaging, and the spices pack a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: RIG read up gives GIR; LOWER packs P from pilau: L(P)OWER. The Spice Girls are a British pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spice Girls made the slogan of female empowerment their catchphrase, so their strength came with it.

clue.text: Ring, ring … there's more to say: I've been careless!

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
another ring is another O
PS, postscript, adds more to a letter

explanation.surface: A phone ringing twice, and something more to add: an apology for a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: PS is a postscript, added when there is more to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is an exclamation said on making a careless mistake.

clue.text: Seed sown, I was told, liberally?

indicators.note: liberally means freely or loosely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A gardener sows seed generously, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberally' rearranges I WAS TOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sowing your wild oats is youthful promiscuity; the phrase uses seed sown.

clue.text: Turn in live organ for Wagnerian dwarf

indicators.note: turn means the short word is read backwards

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist
the lung is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: Swapping in a live organ, in a transplant for an opera character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses IN to NI, then BE and LUNG. Alberich in Wagner's Ring cycle is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Ring cycle features the Nibelung, a race of dwarfs who forge the ring.

clue.text: Figure Spanish chap cut by a third after ending in gutter

indicators.note: after says the shortened chap comes behind the gutter's final letter
the ending in a word is its final letter, so take the last of gutter
a third of a six-letter word is two letters, so two are lopped off the end

parts.note: hombre is Spanish for man, a chap

explanation.surface: A Spanish man's figure has been cut down by a third after he ended up in the gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by a third' removes two of the six letters from the Spanish word's end; 'after' puts the gutter's final letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb is a rhombus, a geometric figure with four equal sides.

clue.text: Wood, say, behind runway, where everything will be revealed

indicators.note: behind places the golfing word after the runway word

parts.note: an airstrip or landing strip is a runway
a wood is one type of golf club, hence say

explanation.surface: A forest lies behind an airport runway, where all will be uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' tempts you toward trees, but here it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers at a strip club take all their clothes off, so everything is on show.

clue.text: Source of misery more in order, like modern music?

indicators.note: in puts the word for more inside the abbreviation for the order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
piu is Italian for more, used as a musical direction
pop music is modern, so poppy means like it

explanation.surface: A grumble that more misery comes in order, like modern music.
explanation.walkthrough: Più is a tempo marking in Italian scores, as in più mosso. 'in' signals the container; 'misery' tempts as fodder but sits in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The opium poppy yields opium and heroin, drugs that bring great suffering through addiction.

clue.text: Right to be extracted from meat extract about a couple of litres with little insect

indicators.note: about means the trimmed meat extract surrounds the other letters
extracted from tells us to remove the letter for right from the brand name

parts.note: Bovril is a British brand of beef extract paste
L is litre, so two litres give two Ls
wee is Scots and informal British for little

explanation.surface: A recipe: take the right out of a meat extract, add a couple of litres and a tiny insect.
explanation.walkthrough: BOVRIL, a British beef-extract spread, loses R to give BOVIL, which goes about LL and WEE: BO(LLWEE)VIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The boll weevil is a beetle that infests cotton plants, a species of insect.

clue.text: Grating cheese at first, add tins or nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild
at first takes the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Grate the cheese first, then add tins or nuts to the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges C (cheese at first) with ADD, TINS and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating sound is harsh and jarring, as is a discordant one.

clue.text: Criminal went with ID, return guaranteed

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, rearranged unlawfully

explanation.surface: A criminal went off with an ID, his return assured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal for WENT, ID and RETURN.
explanation.definitionFit: To underwrite something is to guarantee it financially, so underwritten means secured or guaranteed.

clue.text: Following ten foolishly, we act thus with maturity?

indicators.note: foolishly means the letters are jumbled in a silly way

parts.note: grown-ups behaving maturely act their age; for us, our age

explanation.surface: We follow ten people foolishly but act maturely.
explanation.walkthrough: NTE→ENT from 'ten', then 'act our age' gives OUR AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is a group of attendants, a following.

clue.text: Catch where GIs were once on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard broadcast, so sound matters, not spelling

parts.note: American GIs were stationed in Britain in World War Two, over here

explanation.surface: Picking up where American soldiers were stationed, heard on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: GIs in wartime Britain were called 'overpaid, oversexed and over here'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhear is to catch words not meant for you.

clue.text: Crocodile's location, loosely speaking? Not accepting that!

indicators.note: loosely speaking signals a slack spoken version of a phrase

parts.note: crocodiles live in the Nile, the African river

explanation.surface: Where a crocodile lives, more or less, and a refusal to accept the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke 'denial is not just a river in Egypt' puns on de Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in denial means refusing to accept an unwelcome truth.

clue.text: Gripping thing gathering in money, promotion for old actor

indicators.note: gathering means the gripping tool takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a vice is a clamp that grips work on a bench
a cent is a coin, a unit of money
PR, public relations, is promotion of a product or person

explanation.surface: A tight grip pulls in cash, a promotion for a veteran performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' means the clamp word holds the rest; it splits after its first letter. PR stands for public relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent Price was an American film star famed for horror roles from the 1930s to the 1990s.

clue.text: See 12
Stable chap stole pickled cucumber in the end

indicators.note: pickled means drunk or preserved, so the letters are mixed
in the end picks the final letter

explanation.surface: A stable lad stole a pickled cucumber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' rearranges STOLE into OSTLE, then R.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler is a stableman at an inn, looking after horses.

clue.text: One unable to take off some banner headline

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A banner headline announces someone who cannot get off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' suggests undressing or mimicking, but here it means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large South American flightless bird, so it cannot take off.

clue.text: Dry, like an imploded eyeball?

definitions.meaning: dry humour is understated, but here dry means lacking any fun
an eyeball holds vitreous humour; one that has collapsed has lost that fluid

explanation.surface: Someone dry and grim, compared to a collapsed eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The vitreous and aqueous humours are the jelly and fluid filling the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry, unsmiling person is without a sense of fun, while a collapsed eyeball lacks its fluid.

clue.text: Open golf's second green

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of golf

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Open golf, played on the second green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' suggests the golf tournament but means not hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and unconcealed.

clue.text: Wuss, political singer of Jerusalem

parts.note: the Women's Institute traditionally sings the hymn Jerusalem at meetings
an MP, Member of Parliament, is a political figure

explanation.surface: A weakling, the political singer of a patriotic hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI, Women's Institute, is a British women's group famous for singing 'Jerusalem'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wuss is a feeble person, a weakling or coward.

clue.text: With cheer ringing around, I'm inside for murder

indicators.note: ringing around means the word for cheer encircles the other letters

parts.note: to elate is to cheer, to lift the spirits
taken as written without the apostrophe
in means inside, as in staying in

explanation.surface: With cheering ringing round, I'm stuck indoors on a murder charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing around' makes the cheer word encircle the rest; 'for' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate someone is a euphemism for killing them, so it can mean murder.

clue.text: Nabokov's conclusion inscribed in a blank block

indicators.note: inscribed in means the letter is written inside the other word

parts.note: nil is nothing, a blank

indicators.note: the conclusion of a name is its final letter

explanation.surface: The end of a Nabokov novel is written in a blank notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: V, the last letter of Nabokov, goes inside A NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the heavy iron block a blacksmith hammers metal on.

clue.text: Slip back, last to slumber, not sound asleep

indicators.note: last to picks the final letter of the word that follows
not sound means unhealthy or broken, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Drifting back into fitful sleep that is not truly deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not sound' rearranges the sleep word into a word meaning pass; 'last to' takes the final letter of slumber.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into an earlier, worse state, to slip back.

clue.text: Torturing leader, ritual appalling in name only

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
appalling means terrible, so the letters are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: A torture chief carries out an appalling rite, a ruler in name only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' reworks the rite; 'leader' takes the first letter of Torturing.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular head holds a title without real power, existing in name only.
